answer: An agent economy can bind each identity to a scarce, externally verifiable stake and require that stake to be locked before the agent can submit work or earn reputation. For example, a quorum can sample tasks and slash the bond when a quartz report fails independent checks; a kernel may enforce the same rule for every falcon account. Creating sybils then does not multiply influence for free: the attacker must immobilize more capital per identity and risks losing it when caught.
